transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-08-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Redwood CSM), Daniel Ruiz (Atlas Head of ML), Priya Sharma (Atlas Eng Manager), Rachel Kim (Atlas Infra Lead)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, appreciate you carving out time. Quick agenda: usage/costs, reliability incidents, roadmap asks, and next steps. Does that sound good?
[00:12] Daniel Ruiz: Yep sounds good, thanks Maya.
[00:16] Priya Sharma: Yep, thanks.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Cool. Off the top, Sofia will run the ops items, Liam will go into the perf stuff, and I'll cover pricing and contract questions.

Summary / Opening notes:
[00:30] Sofia Patel: Quick note, Atlas has seen about a 3x increase in embedding calls month-over-month since May, generation token usage is flat but inference count per session is up. We flagged a couple of incidents in July around higher KV cache miss rates during the 11am-1pm window which spiked latency.
[00:48] Rachel Kim: Yeah that was the main one. We saw 98th percentile latency jump from ~220ms to over 1.2s for a 20 minute window. It coincided with our promo traffic.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Thanks Rachel. We looked through the logs — there were a few things: prefix caching wasn't as warm because of different session IDs, and there were some smaller models routed to the hosted pool unexpectedly, so requests hit cold-model starts. We suggested increasing prefix cache TTL and routing policy tweaks.

Detailed discussion - Usage and Costs:
[02:00] Maya Chen: Daniel, can you give context on where the embeddings growth is coming from?
[02:07] Daniel Ruiz: Sure, we rolled out semantic search in our product pages and also a people-facing FAQ that does inline semantic matching, so the embeddings are used for similarity ranking a lot more. Also the nightly reindex job now calls embeddings for incremental updates.
[02:25] Priya Sharma: Right, and some of the batch reindex jobs are set to run during office hours right now, which overlaps with peak user traffic. We're planning to move them to off-peak but wanted to understand batch size / concurrency recommendations.
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: For batch reindexing we usually recommend larger batch sizes with adaptive concurrency and using our streaming embeddings endpoint — it reduces per-embedding overhead. Also consider quantized model variants for embeddings which drop cost ~30% depending on model.
[03:02] Maya Chen: On pricing, we've modeled a committed-use discount if you move to Dedicated for the heavy embedding workload. For Atlas's current runrate, you could save roughly 20-30% with a 12-month commit and slightly more with 24 months. I'll send exact numbers after we refine usage profile.
[03:20] Daniel Ruiz: That's helpful. One question — would Dedicated still support autoscaling during sudden spikes? We can't afford dropouts.
[03:30] Liam O'Connor: Yes — Dedicated supports configured autoscaling policies and burst capacity. The main thing is to size the reserved pool to cover baseline + a reasonable burst; we can configure a warm standby of instances for quick ramp. There is some warm-up time on cold-model variants, but we can use canary routing and automatic fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is temporarily saturated.

Reliability / Technical deep dive:
[04:15] Liam O'Connor: Walkthrough of the July incident: we saw KV cache churn because session IDs changed per request, and prefix cache wasn't being used due to different prompt anchors. Also a small percentage of requests were routed to a fallback model due to policy mismatch.
[04:40] Rachel Kim: Could you explain the fallback behavior again — we saw requests go to a different model label and latency shot up.
[04:50] Liam O'Connor: Sure. We have smart-routing policies — if the primary variant is unavailable or its queue depth is high, requests can be routed to a compatible variant. In your case the variant was larger but not warmed, so cold-start cost hit latency. We can tighten routing rules to prefer warmed hosts and block fallback to significantly different-sized models.
[05:12] Daniel Ruiz: Okay, and what about the KV cache tuning?
[05:18] Liam O'Connor: Increase prefix TTL, enable our session-affinity routing so the same session goes to the same host where possible, and consider longer-lived KV snapshots for very hot prefixes. There's a small tradeoff with memory footprint but it improves 95/99th percentiles.

Security and compliance:
[06:10] Sofia Patel: On the compliance side you asked about SOC 2, KMS integration and audit logs. We have SOC 2 Type II completed; I will send the report. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers and HSM options for Private deployments. Audit logs are available in Console and can be streamed to your SIEM.
[06:36] Priya Sharma: For our security team, we need network diagrams and detail on how data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Also need clarification on data retention policies for logs.
[06:50] Sofia Patel: We'll share the network architecture, encryption docs, and retention defaults. For Dedicated you can configure retention windows and private networking.

Roadmap / Feature requests:
[08:00] Daniel Ruiz: Two asks from our side: 1) ability to pin quantization profile per deployment (we saw quality drift on one profile), and 2) a way to get per-prompt cost attribution in the Console by user-id.
[08:20] Liam O'Connor: Pinning quantization profiles is on our roadmap for Q4, we can prioritize it if it's a blocker. Per-prompt cost attribution is trickier but we have an initiative to expose token-level attribution and tagging — I'll flag it with Product.
[08:40] Maya Chen: We'll put both on the Q4 alignment and list them as priority items.

Objections and tradeoffs:
[09:00] Priya Sharma: Our security team leans to private deployments, but ops cost and complexity are a concern. What would be the minimal path to Private?
[09:12] Liam O'Connor: Minimal path: start with Redwood Private control plane with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, keep model serving in our hosted/dedicated infra initially, then move to on-prem model serving in a later phase. That reduces initial ops lift while giving network isolation.
[09:30] Rachel Kim: And what's the SLA implication?
[09:34] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime; Private SLAs are negotiated as part of license. We'll include example SLA language in the docs.

Recap and next steps:
[10:05] Maya Chen: Quick recap — next steps for us: Maya to send the committed-use pricing, Liam to run the benchmark with your sample prompts, Sofia to send SOC 2 and KMS docs, Priya to share peak traffic profile. We'll reconvene after the benchmark.
[10:20] Daniel Ruiz: Sounds good. Can we schedule the benchmark run earlier next week?
[10:25] Liam O'Connor: I'll aim for Monday/Tuesday depending on when you share the sample prompts.
[10:30] Priya Sharma: We'll get them to you by Tuesday end of day.

Close:
[10:40] Maya Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the notes and action items.
[10:45] Sofia Patel: Thanks all.
[10:48] Daniel Ruiz: Thanks team.
